# owner: platform
"""Contact sheet rows for substitute teachers."""

from typing import List, Sequence

from rosterkit.errors import ProjectError
from rosterkit.models import Student


def contact_rows(*, students: Sequence[Student]) -> List[str]:
    """Text rows of name, section and email, sorted by name."""
    if not students:
        raise ProjectError("no students to build a contact sheet")
    for student in students:
        if not (student.email or "").strip():
            raise ProjectError(
                f"no email for {student.display_name}"
            )
    ordered = sorted(
        students, key=lambda item: (item.display_name, item.student_id)
    )
    name_width = max(len(item.display_name) for item in ordered)
    section_width = max(len(item.section) for item in ordered)
    result = [
        f"{item.display_name:<{name_width}}  "
        f"{item.section:<{section_width}}  "
        f"{item.email.strip()}"
        for item in ordered
    ]
    return result
EOF
cat > tests/test_contacts.py <<'EOF'
# owner: platform
import unittest

from rosterkit.contacts import contact_rows
from rosterkit.errors import ProjectError
from rosterkit.models import Student


def make(student_id, last, first, section, email):
    return Student(student_id, last, first, section, email)


class ContactRowsTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_when_students_are_unsorted_rows_are_sorted(self):
        rows = contact_rows(
            students=[
                make("2", "Varrow", "Ines", "A", "i@x.org"),
                make("1", "Quillon", "Sefa", "A", "s@x.org"),
            ]
        )
        self.assertTrue(rows[0].startswith("Quillon, Sefa"))
        self.assertTrue(rows[1].startswith("Varrow, Ines"))

    def test_when_names_differ_in_length_columns_line_up(self):
        rows = contact_rows(
            students=[
                make("1", "Li", "Al", "A", "a@x.org"),
                make("2", "Thistle", "Bram", "B2", "b@x.org"),
            ]
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            rows[0].index("a@x.org"), rows[1].index("b@x.org")
        )
        self.assertEqual(rows[0].index("A "), rows[1].index("B2"))

    def test_when_email_is_missing_error_names_student(self):
        students = [
            make("1", "Quillon", "Sefa", "A", "s@x.org"),
            make("2", "Thistle", "Bram", "A", None),
        ]
        with self.assertRaises(ProjectError) as caught:
            contact_rows(students=students)
        self.assertIn("Thistle, Bram", str(caught.exception))

    def test_when_email_is_blank_error_names_student(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ProjectError) as caught:
            contact_rows(
                students=[make("2", "Thistle", "Bram", "A", "  ")]
            )
        self.assertIn("Thistle, Bram", str(caught.exception))

    def test_when_list_is_empty_an_error_is_raised(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ProjectError):
            contact_rows(students=[])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
EOF

trace.final_message:
I added `rosterkit/contacts.py` with `contact_rows(*, students)` and committed it as 298d653. The full suite passes (31 tests, including the new ones), and the lint check is clean.

The function returns one text row per student, sorted by display name. Each row has the name, section and email, and the columns are padded to the widest value in each. Students with the same name are ordered by student id.

It raises `ProjectError` in two cases. An empty list gives "no students to build a contact sheet". A student whose email is missing or only whitespace gives "no email for Last, First", so the message names that student. I chose `ProjectError` because it is the project's existing error type, but it is documented as meaning a file is unusable as a whole. Say so if you'd rather have a different exception.

The five new tests are in `tests/test_contacts.py`. They cover sorting, column alignment, a missing email, a blank email and an empty list.

I followed the project notes while writing it:
- The new files start with `# owner: platform`.
- New lines are 72 characters or fewer.
- Test names start with `test_when_`.
- The function has a single return and takes keyword-only parameters.
- The commit subject starts with `chg: ` and ends with `Risk: low`.

I did not export `contact_rows` from `rosterkit/__init__.py`, so it is imported from `rosterkit.contacts`. I can add it to the package exports if you want.
